citations.description: Regression test reproduces the proven mechanism (delete loose object -> merge) and verifies forensics are captured — but this is a test of the instrumentation, not a fix of the root cause.

Ticket comment (timestamp 1786694515415122001): 'Disposition mirrors precedent bug warmthless-dermal-oropendola (relates_to): instrumentation-only close after hypothesis exhaustion... If it recurs: reopen, read the forensic block in the CI log, and root-cause from there.'

findings.criterion: Bug 'Verified-matrix authorship fixture: freshly committed blob missing at merge (invalid object at write-tree)' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.
findings.detail: The implementation is instrumentation-only: _GitFailed now captures object-store forensics (fsck, count-objects, objects listing, GIT_* env) at failure time, but the root cause of the intermittent ENOENT on a freshly committed loose blob was never identified. The ticket explicitly states the organic deleter was not found after 210+ fixture instantiations, and the disposition is 'If it recurs: reopen, read the forensic block in the CI log, and root-cause from there.' The defect (intermittent CI failure with 'invalid object ... git write-tree failed to write a tree') can still reproduce; only the diagnostic capability has been improved. The acceptance criteria themselves do not claim the bug is fixed — they claim hypotheses were killed and instrumentation was landed — but the standard bug-resolution criterion (defect no longer reproduces, expected behavior holds) is not met.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
